answer: Tie rewards to stake that new identities cannot borrow from each other. Picture a jetty where every boat must tie up with its own rope: an agent's earnings stay locked for weeks and are only released after unrelated peers keep confirming its work. One operator cannot cheaply spin up a fleet, because each clone needs its own pearl of locked value, and an atlas of who-attested-whom makes tight rings that only vouch for each other easy to spot and slash.
